name: Angkor Wat
summary: The largest religious monument on Earth — a 12th-century Khmer masterpiece rising from the jungle near Siem Reap.

body: Angkor Wat is the centrepiece of the Angkor Archaeological Park near Siem Reap — a 12th-century Khmer temple-mountain dedicated first to Vishnu, later embraced as a Buddhist sanctuary. Its five lotus towers, moat, and kilometres of bas-reliefs make it one of the world’s most recognisable sacred monuments.
A visit rewards slow walking: galleries of the Hindu epics, quiet courtyards, and the long causeway at dawn. Plan it as part of a multi-day Angkor Pass rather than a single rushed hour.
highlights: Largest religious monument complex on Earth
Best with a licensed guide on a multi-day pass

visit.intro: The Angkor Pass covers Angkor Wat and 50+ temples in the park. Hours and booth rules shift seasonally — confirm before you go.
visit.hours: Park access commonly from around sunrise; individual temples may open/close on staggered schedules. Ticket booths and online purchase windows differ from temple opening times — verify the day before.
visit.tickets: 1-, 3-, and 7-day Angkor Passes are required for foreigners. Buy only via Angkor Enterprise (official site, app, kiosk, or counter). Third-party “cheap” passes are often invalid.
visit.dress: Cover shoulders and knees. Hats off in shrine spaces. Sturdy shoes for uneven laterite and steep steps.
visit.duration: Half day for the main Angkor Wat circuit; 2–3 days for the wider park without rushing.
visit.access: Long causeway and galleries involve stairs and uneven stone. Upper towers are often restricted; skip climbs if mobility is limited.
tips: Carry water, sun protection, and small cash for vendors.
Keep your pass visible — checks are frequent.
Hire a tuk-tuk or car for the day rather than hopping ad hoc.
visit.ticketsNote: Official Angkor Enterprise — check current 1/3/7-day prices on the site before paying. Avoid unofficial resellers.

etiquette.intro: Angkor Wat is both a monument and a living place of devotion. Treat towers, monks, and worshippers with care.
bullets: Do not climb on restricted towers, lintels, or bas-reliefs.
Keep voices low near active shrines and monks.
Ask before photographing people at prayer.
Drones are restricted — check current park rules before packing one.
Dress codes are enforced at many towers; carry a light scarf or wrap.

gettingThere.intro: Most visitors base in Siem Reap and enter the park by tuk-tuk, car, or bicycle with a pass.
paragraphs: Fly into Siem Reap–Angkor International Airport (SAI). From central Siem Reap, Angkor Wat is roughly 20–30 minutes by tuk-tuk depending on traffic and which gate you use.
Licensed guides and fixed-price day drivers are widely available; agree the circuit (Angkor Wat + Angkor Thom + Ta Prohm is the classic first day) before you leave town.
bullets: Nearest hub: Siem Reap (SAI airport + town hotels)
Typical last mile: tuk-tuk or private car with Angkor Pass
Cycling is possible for nearby temples if you are fit and heat-aware

bestTime.intro: Cooler, drier months are kinder for long stone walks; sunrise is beautiful and crowded.
paragraphs: November–February is the classic high season: clearer skies and cooler mornings. March–May bring heat; June–October bring rain and lush vegetation with fewer crowds on some days.
Sunrise at the reflecting pools is iconic — arrive early, then linger for quieter mid-morning galleries after tour groups move on.
bullets: Best overall: November–February
Hottest: April–May — start at dawn
Festivals and public holidays increase crowds — verify local calendars

notes.intro: 注意事項 · Verify before visit — park rules and ticket systems change.
bullets: Confirm opening hours and pass rules the day before — seasonal changes are common.
Many towers have steep, uneven steps without handrails.
Heat exhaustion is real: shade, water, and a midday rest help.
Respect rope barriers and restoration zones — they protect fragile stone.

name: Borobudur
summary: A vast 9th-century Mahayana Buddhist stupa-temple — terraces of stone reliefs ascending toward a silent, misty summit.

body: Borobudur is a 9th-century Mahayana Buddhist monument in Central Java — concentric terraces of stone reliefs ascending toward a silent stupa summit.
Access rules have tightened: courtyard tickets and temple-climb tickets differ, and upper levels may require timed entry.
highlights: Sunrise tickets sold separately when offered

visit.dress: Modest clothing. Temple cloth (sarong) may be required for upper levels — usually provided with climb tickets.
visit.duration: 2–3 hours including museum and grounds; longer with sunrise.
visit.access: Many steps and uneven stone. Upper terraces may close or limit numbers.
tips: Book climb slots ahead in peak season.

name: Meiji Shrine
summary: A forest sanctuary in central Tokyo dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken — quiet paths, towering torii, living tradition.

body: Meiji Jingū is a Shinto shrine set in a man-made forest in central Tokyo, dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken.
Grounds are free. Inner garden tickets and special exhibitions are separate when offered.

summary: The holiest gurdwara of Sikhism — a gold-clad sanctuary in a sacred pool, open to all who come with respect.

body: Harmandir Sahib — the Golden Temple — is the holiest gurdwara of Sikhism: a gold-clad sanctum in the Amrit Sarovar, open to everyone who enters with respect.
The visit is spiritual first. Cover your head, remove shoes, and consider joining langar, the community kitchen that feeds all.

visit.access: Marble paths can be wet and crowded. Ask about accessible routes at entrances.
